## Ecuador Tour Featuring a Butterfly Farm on the Napo River

During a stay in the Ecuadorian Amazon, visitors can see butterflies in a living exhibit near Casa del Suizo Lodge. The standalone [“Butterfly Farm near Casa del Suizo” excursion](/ecuador/napo-river/casa-del-suizo-butterfly-farm/) introduces the insects' stages of development, from early life to the adult butterfly, and invites guests into a spacious enclosed area where dozens or hundreds of butterflies fly among plants.

The excursion is one of the possible choices for an Amazonian day on the [“Ecuador: Andes, Amazon and Galápagos” tour from September 1 to 11, 2027](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/). It is an independent thematic module within a longer journey, not a separate multi-day tour to a butterfly farm.

**Amazonian activities are selected from several available options.** A link to the butterfly farm in the program does not mean travelers will necessarily visit it alongside the forest trail, river island, and other excursions. The content of the Amazonian day must be agreed before the trip.

## What You Can See at the Butterfly Farm

The farm is approximately **15 minutes on foot from Casa del Suizo**. It houses more than 20 local species. Visitors learn how butterflies develop and are raised, then observe them in an enclosure filled with live plants. The bright-blue **morpho** is among the well-known species mentioned.

This setting lets you study insects more closely than on an ordinary tropical forest trail and understand the differences between stages of their life cycle. The main value of the excursion lies in observation and explanations, making it suitable for discovering the region's nature even without a long hike.

It is a living exhibit for visitors, not a guarantee of seeing a particular number of butterflies at any one moment. The number of visible individuals and their activity may vary; conditions for each visit are determined locally.

## Where the Farm Fits into the Ecuador Itinerary

The [11-day program](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/) starts with Quito and the Andean highlands, followed by [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) and a transfer to the [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/). The Amazon section includes **2 nights at Casa del Suizo Lodge**.

On **day 6**, travelers stay in the lodge area and choose activities with local guides. The butterfly farm is among the modules available on that day. On the following day, the itinerary heads toward the [Papallacta hot springs](/ecuador/place/papallacta/) and then onward to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

A farm visit offers a chance to focus on one small nature story amid a varied journey: travelers have already seen the Andes, are staying beside the Amazon rainforest, and will soon encounter an entirely different island ecosystem. For people interested in wildlife, these observations complement a trip through several of Ecuador's natural regions.

## Choosing Among Other Casa del Suizo Excursions

The butterfly farm and the [Misicocha Reserve walk](/ecuador/misicocha-reserve/ecuador-misicocha-forest-walk/) explore different aspects of nature. At the farm, visitors learn about insect development and examine butterflies in a dedicated enclosure. In Misicocha, they walk along rainforest trails, listen to a local guide, and learn about trees and plants in their natural habitat.

Another option is the [river island walk](/ecuador/napo-river/casa-del-suizo-river-island-walk/). Visitors are shown crops cultivated by local people: cassava, bananas, cacao, and coffee. If observing butterflies is your main interest, the farm is the natural choice; for more extensive physical activity, choose the trail; and to learn about crops and local livelihoods, visit the river island.

| Interest | Where to go |
|---|---|
| Butterfly species and development | Casa del Suizo farm |
| Humid forest trails | Misicocha |
| Cassava, bananas, cacao | River island near Casa del Suizo |

The full range of available options can vary depending on how the day is organized. This is particularly important to confirm when traveling with children or when physical exertion and walking distances need to be limited.

## What the Journey Includes and How Much It Costs

The tour from **September 1–11, 2027** lasts **11 days and 10 nights**. It covers the highlands, Amazon lodge, Papallacta's thermal region, and the Galápagos Islands. Our tour costs **4260 USD per person in double occupancy**; alternative accommodation options are shown on the [tour page](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/).

Paying for the entire journey and any admission charge for the specific farm are separate issues. The lodge's own official program lists the breeding facility among activities that may involve additional entrance fees. For the Ada Tours option, you need to confirm whether visiting the farm is included in the selected price calculation. The overall tour price also excludes international and domestic flights, insurance, and entry to Galápagos National Park.

The tour suits people interested in Ecuador's nature as a whole: the rainforest portion lasts 2 nights, with the rest of the trip divided between the Andes and islands. If you want a journey devoted exclusively to the Amazon, compare other [Ecuador itineraries](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Butterfly Farm Tour

### Which Tour Includes This Excursion?

The butterfly farm is listed among the possible excursions on **day 6** of the current “Ecuador: Andes, Amazon and Galápagos” tour, September 1–11, 2027.

### How Do You Reach the Farm?

According to the excursion description, it is about **15 minutes' walk** from Casa del Suizo in the Napo River area.

### Which Butterflies Can You See There?

More than 20 local species live in the facility, including the blue morpho. The farm introduces visitors to butterfly life cycles, although seeing every particular species on one visit cannot be guaranteed.

### Can You Combine the Farm with a Forest Walk?

Both activities appear on the Amazonian day's list. The program involves **choosing among routes**, so any combination must be agreed with the organizer based on timing and actual availability.

### Is Farm Admission Included in the Total Price?

The tour page does not separately confirm the price of admission to this farm. Whether it is included in your selected package is established when the Amazonian day's activities are agreed.

## River Island Walk near Casa del Suizo: Amazonian Plants in 1–2 Hours

The [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/) forms islands and floodplain areas where tropical vegetation grows alongside crops cultivated by local people. On our excursion near Casa del Suizo, a river crossing is followed by **an easy walk lasting about 1–2 hours**. It is an opportunity to learn which plants are grown in the Ecuadorian Amazon and where they occur outside plantations.

There is no demanding trek, climb, or lengthy rafting trip advertised here. The excursion centers on a leisurely introduction to plants and explanations from the local guide.

## Plants Along the Route

During the walk, you learn about **cassava (yuca), bananas, cacao, coffee, herbs, and tuber crops**. Local people cultivate some of them; others grow in the wild. It is especially interesting for travelers to see familiar food products growing before they are processed and appear in a kitchen.

**Cassava** is a root crop widespread across tropical South America. Your guide may explain how it is grown and why local communities use it as food. Bananas and other edible crops demonstrate how closely the island landscape is linked to people's daily lives.

**Cacao** and **coffee** add a culinary dimension, but seeing them along the route **does not confirm a separate tasting, chocolate-making workshop, or coffee farm visit**. What is specifically described for this excursion is discovering cultivated plants and their natural surroundings.

## The Route After the River Crossing

First, the group crosses the river to reach the island. Then comes a walk with stops and explanations about plants. We offer **a straightforward 1–2-hour walking experience**; the distance, crossing arrangements, and trail conditions have not been specified in detail beforehand.

Rainfall and water levels on the Napo may affect access to riverbanks, so the actual route depends on current conditions. Different forest types occur in the river valley, including seasonally flooded areas; you should not assume every island is permanently dry or walkable in all weather.

Bring closed-toe shoes with nonslip soles, rain protection, water, and insect repellent. Do not leave the route or taste unfamiliar fruits without your local guide's advice.

## How the River Island Differs from the Butterfly Farm

Both excursions explore the natural environment of the Ecuadorian Amazon, but they answer different questions. On the river island, attention is devoted to **plants, agricultural crops, and how people use them**. At the nearby [Casa del Suizo butterfly farm](/ecuador/napo-river/casa-del-suizo-butterfly-farm/), visitors discover insect development stages and observe living butterflies in a special enclosure.

The island walk can be treated as a standalone nature-learning activity and the butterfly farm as a separate addition. We do not promise that both sites are automatically included within one paid excursion.

## What Is Included, and Who Will Enjoy It?

The route is intended for travelers who want to explore the Amazon without substantial athletic exertion. A duration of **1–2 hours** suits a short outing near the lodge, but the river crossing and humid conditions still require ordinary precautions.

**No fixed price, complete list of services, or separate meal-inclusion condition is specified** for this excursion. The guiding arrangements, crossing cost, and any optional activities are established for the particular offer. The lodge's program may include other activities, but they are not automatically added to this excursion.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Casa del Suizo River Island

### How Long Does the Walk Take?

Approximately **1–2 hours** after crossing to the island. The duration may depend on river conditions and the group's pace.

### Which Crops Do Visitors See?

The description lists cassava, bananas, cacao, coffee, herbs, and tuber plants. The guide explains local farming and the surrounding vegetation.

### Is Chocolate Tasting Included?

It is not listed in the excursion description. Cacao growing along the route does not automatically mean a tasting or workshop is included.

### Is Special Training Necessary?

No demanding athletic training is specified. Simply account for humid weather, the river crossing, and the guide's safety instructions.

## Tour Featuring a River Island Walk near Casa del Suizo

The [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/) is one of the main waterways of the Ecuadorian Amazon. Forest areas, communities, and small farming plots lie near its banks and lodges. During the [Casa del Suizo river island walk](/ecuador/napo-river/casa-del-suizo-river-island-walk/), travelers cross the river and then discover the region's plants with a local guide.

The excursion lasts around **1–2 hours**. It is interesting because you can see how familiar products such as cacao, coffee, and bananas grow in a tropical climate. The guide also explains cassava, other tuber plants, and herbs. Local people cultivate some species, while others occur in the wild.

This module appears among the Amazonian options in the [“Ecuador: Andes, Amazon and Galápagos” tour, September 1–11, 2027](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/). Importantly, day six includes **a choice of excursions**: not every listed activity can be regarded as a guaranteed part of a single day's itinerary.

## How the Island Walk Unfolds

Travelers first cross the river, then follow a relatively easy route with a guide. The main subjects are local crops and plants, so the excursion differs from long trekking routes through the forest. You can discover how cassava and other tubers are used, how bananas and cacao are cultivated, and which plants matter to the livelihoods of Amazonian communities.

The standalone excursion lasts **about 1–2 hours**. Trail conditions depend on the weather and water levels. During the rainy season, the crossing and order of stops are determined by local conditions.

A river island walk is **not the same thing** as a rafting trip. A balsa raft is mentioned as a possible continuation of the [Misicocha forest walk](/ecuador/misicocha-reserve/ecuador-misicocha-forest-walk/). The island module has a different central purpose: walking and discovering cultivated plants.

## When the Island Can Be Visited During the Tour

Our itinerary lasts **11 days and 10 nights**. Early in the journey, travelers explore Quito, Quilotoa Lake, and [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). The Amazonian section then begins, including **2 nights at Casa del Suizo Lodge**. The [Napo](/ecuador/place/napo-river/) area, reached by boat, provides the starting point for river outings.

On **day 6**, after breakfast, travelers are offered activities with local guides. Options include the river island excursion, [butterfly farm](/ecuador/napo-river/casa-del-suizo-butterfly-farm/), the Misicocha forest trail, introductions to local traditions, and other attractions. The number of activities completed that day depends on the selected itinerary.

On the following day, the journey continues to the [Papallacta hot springs](/ecuador/place/papallacta/). Later comes a visit to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), where the focus shifts to a completely different island ecosystem. The Napo island walk occupies a relatively small part of the overall itinerary but provides meaningful insight into everyday life in the Amazon region.

## How the Island Differs from Other Amazonian Activities

| Excursion | Main interest |
|---|---|
| River island | Cassava, cacao, bananas, local crops |
| [Misicocha](/ecuador/misicocha-reserve/ecuador-misicocha-forest-walk/) | Tropical forest and walking trails |
| [Butterfly farm](/ecuador/napo-river/casa-del-suizo-butterfly-farm/) | Butterfly development and observation |

A long hike is not the main objective of the island walk. It suits travelers interested in botany in a practical sense: where food comes from, which plants local communities use, and how agriculture works in a tropical region.

If you would rather follow a forest path, consider Misicocha, with walks lasting from 1 to 4 hours. Butterfly enthusiasts may prefer the breeding facility. When choosing activities for one excursion day, prioritize the experience that best matches your interests and available time.

## Choosing the Tour and Understanding the Price

The Ada Tours program for 2027 lists a group departure on **September 1–11**, covering several natural regions of Ecuador. The base price is **4260 USD per person in double occupancy**. Rates for other accommodation arrangements are detailed on the [“Ecuador: Andes, Amazon and Galápagos” tour page](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/).

This amount covers the multi-day journey; it is not the price of a standalone river island walk. International and domestic air tickets, insurance, and the Galápagos National Park admission fee are paid separately on the larger tour. Before booking, confirm your selected Casa del Suizo activities and the exact services included in the Amazonian day.

If you want to spend more time in river and forest regions, compare [all Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/). On the itinerary described here, the Amazon receives 2 nights, followed by travel through the highlands and islands.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the River Island Tour

### How Long Is the Walk?

The standalone Casa del Suizo river island excursion is described as **an easy 1–2-hour walk** after the river crossing.

### What Can You Learn During the Excursion?

The guide introduces cassava, bananas, cacao, coffee, herbs, and other plants used by local communities or found growing in the wild.

### On Which Day of the Larger Tour Does the Excursion Take Place?

It appears among the options for **day 6** of the September 1–11, 2027 journey through Ecuador. The specific choice of activities is agreed with the organizer.

### Is This a Rafting Excursion?

No. The river island is explored on foot after crossing the river. Rafting on a balsa raft belongs to a different possible activity near Casa del Suizo.

### Can the Island and Misicocha Be Visited Together?

Both are listed among possible Amazonian excursions. Combining them in one day is not guaranteed in advance and depends on the selected itinerary and local conditions.

## Visiting a Kichwa Family: Chicha and Crafts on the Napo River

Our excursion explores the everyday skills and traditions of people living in the Ecuadorian Amazon. After a short boat trip downstream, travelers meet a Kichwa family, discover the local drink **chicha**, and visit pottery and woodcarving workshops on the return journey.

Unlike a nature excursion through the forest, this experience centers on **conversation with people and discovering the skills they practice by hand**. River transfers are simply the way to move between stops in the [Napo](/ecuador/place/napo-river/) area.

## Why Taste Chicha?

Chicha is a traditional drink made in various ways by different communities. During the visit, you learn how the Kichwa family prepares chicha and have the opportunity to taste it. Its exact ingredients, fermentation method, and alcohol content are not specified in the excursion details, so people with dietary restrictions should ask their hosts or guide before tasting.

The central value of the visit is to see an everyday tradition in its own context, rather than treating the tasting as a separate restaurant activity. If you would prefer not to sample the drink, discuss this calmly and respectfully with the family and organizer in advance.

## The Blowgun: Discovering a Traditional Hunting Skill

Guests hear about the blowgun traditionally used for hunting by people living in the rainforest. Anyone interested can **try hitting a target**. This is a demonstration of a skill within a cultural program, not a hunting expedition.

The guides on site determine how visitors may participate and the appropriate safe distance. Respect for the hosts' explanations and rules matters more than attempting the exercise at all costs.

## Pottery and Wooden Bird Figurines

The return journey includes **two distinct craft experiences**. At a pottery workshop, a craftswoman demonstrates how traditional objects are shaped by hand from natural materials available in the Oriente region. The group then visits a woodcarving workshop, where visitors can watch bird figurines being made.

Both stops show the difference between the techniques used to make ceramic vessels and the artistic shaping of wood. Ask separately whether you can make an object yourself: the excursion includes **demonstrations by artisans**, but we do not promise a hands-on workshop for every guest.

Purchases of finished products should not be assumed to be included. If you want to take home the work of a local craftsperson, consider in advance how to pack fragile pottery safely for the rest of your travels.

## Visiting a Family and Workshops Respectfully

Ask permission before photographing people, homes, and work processes. In small family workshops, it is especially important to let the hosts decide what they are comfortable showing.

Light clothing, sun and insect protection, and comfortable shoes for boarding a boat are useful in this tropical region. Electronics need protection from water. **The precise excursion duration has not been specified**, so allow for boat transfers and stops before fitting it between tightly scheduled appointments.

This option suits travelers interested in [culture and history](/interests/culture-and-history/) and local [culinary traditions](/interests/food-and-wine/). Compare other activities and nature routes in the [Ecuador excursion catalog](/ecuador/excursion/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Visiting a Kichwa Family

### What Does the Excursion Include?

A family visit, explanations of chicha preparation, tasting, a blowgun demonstration, and stops at pottery and woodcarving workshops.

### Is Tasting Chicha Mandatory?

The description offers the opportunity to taste the drink. Discuss its ingredients and any personal restrictions before sampling it.

### Can I Make a Craft Item Myself?

The excursion confirms demonstrations by artisans. Hands-on participation by every guest in pottery or carving is not separately promised.

### How Long Does the Visit Last?

No exact duration is set in the published excursion description. It depends on boat transfer times and the agreed program.

## Tours Visiting a Kichwa Family on the Napo River: Where the Visit Takes Place and How the Itinerary Works

Visiting a Kichwa family on the Napo River suits travelers who want to discover life in an Amazonian community and traditional crafts as part of a longer trip through Ecuador. In our selection, this excursion is linked to the [“Ecuador: Andes, Amazon and Galápagos” group itinerary from September 1–11, 2027](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/). The journey lasts 11 days and 10 nights, with stops in the highlands, Amazon, and [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

The main difference from a standalone cultural outing is that the Kichwa family visit appears among the optional excursion modules during the Amazon portion. When planning, it is important to agree which lodge activities to choose, how much time is available for each, and how they fit into the main itinerary.

## What You Will Discover During the Kichwa Family Visit

The [Kichwa family excursion](/ecuador/napo-river/ecuador-kichwa-family-crafts/) begins with a short journey downstream by boat. The hosts demonstrate how the traditional drink chicha is made and invite guests to taste it. Visitors also learn about the blowgun traditionally used for hunting and can try hitting a target.

On the return journey, there are visits to a pottery workshop where objects are made by hand and a woodcarving workshop that produces, among other things, bird figurines. These are distinct crafts: the preparation of a local drink, pottery, and carving complement one another. The excursion's own page explains the activities in more detail; here the focus is on where the visit fits into the wider journey.

## When the Visit Takes Place During the 11-Day Journey

The itinerary crosses several natural regions of Ecuador. The group first explores [Quito and the Cotopaxi area](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), then visits [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) and [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). After the mountain roads, travelers descend into the Amazon for two nights at Casa del Suizo Lodge.

The transfer to the Amazon lodge is arranged via Punta Ahuano: from the river landing, guests continue by canoe. On the day devoted to Amazonian activities, the program offers several standalone modules, including the Kichwa family visit, forest walks, and other lodge excursions. **An excursion's presence on the list does not mean that every listed activity will necessarily take place for the whole group.** The specific combination of activities and availability must be agreed before departure.

After the Amazon, travelers head to the Papallacta hot springs and then continue to the Galápagos. The journey therefore gives a relatively short but meaningful introduction to the culture of the Napo region within a much broader itinerary.

## Who Will Enjoy This Option?

This is an appealing choice for people who want to combine nature with culture. In one journey, travelers move from highland regions to humid tropical forests and then to island wildlife. The Amazonian family visit provides insight into everyday local activities, but the tour is not devoted exclusively to ethnography.

If your main objective is to spend several full days in local communities, consider discussing a separate extension of the Amazon portion. If varied landscapes and the Galápagos matter more, the existing 11-day itinerary provides a convenient framework for choosing experiences.

| Part of the itinerary | Main considerations |
|---|---|
| Andes | Cities, altitude, transfers |
| Napo River | Lodge and choice of excursions |
| Papallacta | Thermal relaxation |
| Galápagos | Island program |

## What to Confirm Before Booking

Ask us whether the Kichwa family visit is included among the agreed activities on your selected day. The sequence of transfers also matters: the overland journey to Punta Ahuano, the boat crossing to the lodge, the return to the highlands, and the flight to the islands. You will need clothing for both a warm, humid climate and cooler mountains.

Also compare included services and additional expenses in the [specific tour description](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/). It lists dates, hotels, accommodation options, flights, and guiding arrangements. To choose other itineraries, see the [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours with a Kichwa Family Visit

### Can I Visit a Kichwa Family on a Trip to the Galápagos?

Yes. The September 1–11, 2027 itinerary includes an Amazonian stage and this excursion module. Whether it takes place among the selected activities is confirmed when the itinerary is agreed.

### Does the Excursion Take Place on the Galápagos?

No. The Kichwa family visit takes place in the mainland Amazon, in the [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/) region. The Galápagos form a separate stage after the return from the Amazon.

### Do I Need to Set Aside an Entire Day?

The current 11-day tour includes a day dedicated to Amazonian activities. It offers a choice of lodge experiences; the compatibility of specific excursions is agreed according to the program and time available on site.
